name: Henrietta Ogochukwu Okechukwu
quote: The leaderboard is truly teaching me more patience and deep attention to detail. When the review flagged my progress table as duplicated, it felt a bit awkward at first because I knew I hadn't intentionally set it up that way. But engineering has a way of teaching us skills we didn't know we had. I went back, inspected my README.md, and sure enough, there was an extra table sitting right beneath it! Fixing that made me realize why my review couldn't process. Learning, unlearning, and re-learning has become my pattern, and I am sticking with it.

name: Rohan Kumar Das
quote: I have always been an admirer of transparency, and I can't be more thankful for the level where DMI stands. It's very easy to claim something great, and it's just as hard to maintain. I have seen people raising issues, but at the same time Pravin Sir just magically made the response by making the leaderboard transparent. And the level of transparency is on the next level, where each and every member can know where he or she is lacking, what others did, and why. When truth is accepted, then only progress can begin.
role: System Engineer at Tata Consultancy Services

name: Emmanuel Ulu
quote: There were times during #DMI when I got tired of writing and wished there was never another blog to submit. But looking back now, that consistency changed a lot for me. Technical blogging and documenting my journey helped me understand concepts more deeply, improve my communication skills, increase my visibility in the cloud/community space, and connect with amazing engineers globally. One thing I've learned is that documentation truly compounds over time. A single post may seem small today, but consistency builds credibility, confidence, and opportunities.
role: AWS Community Builder · Cloud & DevOps Engineer

name: Bhupendra Bhati
quote: Technical blogging has been one of the most valuable habits I've developed through DMI. It not only helped me reinforce what I learned in DevOps and Cloud technologies, but also gave me a platform to share my journey, connect with like-minded professionals, and showcase my work publicly. Over time, I noticed improvements in my communication skills, confidence, and ability to explain complex concepts in a simple way. Most importantly, it created a visible record of my growth that opened doors to new opportunities, including becoming an AWS Community Builder.
role: AWS Community Builder · Cloud & DevOps Engineer

name: Ranbir Kaur
quote: During my #DMI journey, we were encouraged to share and document learning publicly. Initially, I believed technical learning was only about completing courses, certifications, and labs. Over time, I realised that writing and explaining concepts helped me improve my understanding. Coming from an Oracle DBA, infrastructure, and support background, I had written a few blogs earlier, but public technical writing was outside my comfort zone. The motivation to write, share, and stay active helped me grow significantly.
role: AWS Community Builder · Cloud & DevOps Engineer

name: Ahanonye Nkechi Anna
quote: Being part of DMI Cohort 1 has been one of the most rewarding learning experiences of my career. There were days of confusion, debugging, failed deployments, and moments when things didn't work as expected, but those moments taught me more than any certificate ever could. Thank you for believing in us, challenging us, and constantly reminding us that mastery is built through consistency, not shortcuts.

name: Pratyush Pahari
quote: I'm one of the 120 students who made it to the final project in DMI Cohort 2.0. DMI is not something you “consume.” It's something you commit to. There were weeks when balancing assignments, live sessions, documentation, debugging, and learning new tools felt overwhelming. But that pressure is exactly what forced growth. The biggest lesson I learned here: consistency beats talent when the goal is to become a DevOps engineer.

name: Love Ogujiofor
quote: You cannot go through this program and remain the same person you were when you started. You stop thinking like someone “learning DevOps” and start thinking like an engineer. There were moments of frustration, moments I doubted myself, and moments I wanted to rest. But looking back now, I can confidently sit in DevOps conversations and understand what is happening because this program forced me to grow through real world engineering experience.

name: Temitayo Ali Awopetu
quote: As a DMI Cohort-2 student, I can confidently say that technical blogging has been one of the most valuable parts of the program. Writing about what I learn has helped me understand concepts more deeply, improve my communication skills, and build a public record of my growth in DevOps. Beyond learning, it has also given me more confidence to share my knowledge and connect with other professionals in the community.
